item.title: I Want to Contribute to a Conversation
item.description:
I want to contribute to a conversation

I’ve been trying to understand what I really want from my career, music, and how i spend my time in general. I love to find a nice coffee shop or restaurant around the east village and write about my thoughts. Thats how I’ve spent a good portion of my free weekends and mornings and evenings since moving to NYC but also for long before then. Doing work and talking about it with friends and other people is such a core part of what i enjoy most in life. Work isn’t necessarily work-work, but just anything that takes some effort to get an interesting outcome. A night at a cocktail bar or a birthday party or a home cooked dinner or ordering furniture are all work that bring joy to my life, and then talking about those things with friends or experiencing them with friends or with co-workers or strangers and understanding what about that work was meaningful and what was funny and what you want to do next is so PEAK life to me.

item.title: Its Easier to Do Things When Youre Not Upset
item.description:
It’s so uninteresting to me to pull up to work being upset about being there every day and moping about the time i have to spend there and being stressed about not having things done.

Firstly, you need to be comfortable with things undone as long as you work towards getting them done. Thats the whole point of having a job. There are undone things that someone needs to do. Firstly, removing the stress and fear about that regular part of the job is big.

item.title: One Person One Thing
item.description:
“he convinced himself, as we all do, that one person or one thing is going to change everything”

This is a quote from a podcast about Scott Pilgrim vs The World. This weekend I’ve been in the mood where every little phrase and song has the chance to ring true with me but this in particular has resonant.

I feel this way because often in my last couple years of struggling with life’s purpose, I keep running up against the idea that there is a single thing I need to do to fix things. I need to make my album or get a new job.

item.title: Who Im Writing For
item.description:
Your audience is one specific person

I heard this in some advice video about writing youtube videos, but I think it’s a pretty common piece of guidance to help write more focused and useful blogs. The wisdom behind it is that if you have one person in mind, it helps you to focus on the needs of that reader in a more imaginative way.

My imaginary reader is going to be myself for now I think. It could also be a friend or family member. But right now I want it to be me because I have a lot of ideas I need to communicate to myself better, funny as it is. I find myself on the cusp of a breakthrough all the time but then the core of what I’m feeling gets lost before I internalize it I think. Even now I’m qualifying this advice with “I thinks” all over the place.

item.title: Other Than the End
item.description:
​ We met to take a walk before you left
​ Was just so glad we’d get to talk again
​ And something on your patient faded breath
​ Had made it even harder to pretend

​ Today was any other than the end
​ The base our careful balance on could should shift
​ Soon as we face each other but instead
​ We fix our gaze at waves beyond the cliff

item.title: Blossoms
item.description:
Couldn’t gather patience in the garden
While they posed for pictures with the blossoms
Until I remembered how important
It was catching my own fleeting moments

When you feel the daylight dying colder
Walking with your love and never knowing
If there is another chance for photos
Blossoms by the winter will be frozen
